This script covers two closely related revision items that share the same input data (the five
validation species' real RepeatMasker per-locus records, `processed_output.temp`, already used
for item 31):

- **Item 32** (R1#2, R1#7): fit skew-normal and gamma distributions, alongside the Gaussian
  currently assumed by modes 0/1/2's identity draw, to the empirical per-family/per-genome
  divergence data, and report KS-statistic/AIC/BIC goodness-of-fit.
- **Item 36** (R2#3): before/after sensitivity check on the `identity_fix` ascertainment-bias
  adjustment (`identity + (100 - identity) * 0.5`) that TEgenomeSimulator <= v1.0.0 applied on
  top of the raw Gaussian draw in `TE_sim_random_insertion.py`'s `generate_sequence()` (and in
  `TE_sim_nested_insertion.py`) - show the identity distribution pre- and post-adjustment against
  the real empirical distribution. The adjustment has since been removed from the simulator
  (commit `efa3369`), partly on the basis of this comparison; the current simulator mutates each
  copy with the raw Gaussian draw directly, so section 3 documents the former behaviour.

Only the **real (original) genome** RepeatMasker data is used below - not mode-2 simulated
output - because both items ask whether the simulator's generative assumption (a Gaussian, and
formerly the `identity_fix` transform) matches real biology, not whether the simulator
reproduces its own input parameters.

How to run:
`sbatch --cpus-per-task=5 --mem=48G -t 1-00:00:00 -J gof_knit -o gof_knit.%j.out -e gof_knit.%j.err --wrap "cd /workspace/cflthc/script/TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/script/revision && Rscript -e \"rmarkdown::render('23.1_item32_divergence_gof.Rmd')\""`

## 0. Setup directory
### 0.1 Setup genome name and directory
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
genomename1a <- 'tair10_original'
genomename2a <- 'rice_original'
genomename3a <- 'maize_original'
genomename4a <- 'dm6_original'
genomename5a <- 'danio_original'

WRK <- "/workspace/cflthc/script"
setwd(WRK)
# results re-generated after the identity sampling/reporting fix
SIM1 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_result/")
SIM2 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/TEgenomeSimulator_rice_result/")
SIM3 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/TEgenomeSimulator_maize_result/")
SIM4 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/TEgenomeSimulator_dm6_result/")
SIM5 <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/TEgenomeSimulator_danio_result/")

OUT <- file.path(WRK, "TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code/output/divergence_gof/")
dir.create(file.path(OUT), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir=OUT)

# Minimum copy number for a family to get its own fit; families below this
# are only included in the genome-pooled fit (section 2.2).
MIN_FAMILY_N <- 30

# Per-family fits are limited to the TOP_N_FAMILY most abundant families (by copy
# number) of each superfamily, and only for superfamilies holding at least
# MIN_SUPERFAMILY_PROP of a genome's loci. A relative threshold is used instead of a
# fixed count (e.g. 1,000 loci) so small genomes keep their main superfamilies
# (tair10 LTR/Copia, dm6 LTR/Copia) while danio's many minor ones are dropped.
TOP_N_FAMILY <- 10
MIN_SUPERFAMILY_PROP <- 0.01

# Superfamily labels left out of the per-family fits (still in the genome-pooled fit):
# class-only or unclassified labels ("DNA", "LTR", "Unknown", "LINE/unknown", "SINE?")
# and non-TE repeats (satellites, simple repeats, rDNA, knobs, centromeric and
# subtelomeric repeats, endogenous viruses).
GENERIC_SF_REGEX <- "^[^/]*$|unknown|\\?"
NON_TE_SF_REGEX <- "^(Satellite|Simple_repeat|Low_complexity|rDNA|rRNA|tRNA|snRNA|scRNA|srpRNA|knob|Cent|Centro|subtelomere|Evirus)(/|$)"

# Fits use a random sample of at most MAX_FIT_N loci per group (fixed seed, so the
# same sample is drawn on every knit); the full n is reported alongside n_fit.
MAX_FIT_N <- 20000
FIT_SEED <- 20261102

# Genomes are processed in parallel (one forked R process per genome)
N_CORES <- 5
```

## 1. Load real per-locus data for the five validation genomes

Same `processed_output.temp` files as item 31 (`identity` is a 0-1 match fraction; `div = 1 -
identity`). `family` and `superfamily` are already present as columns in this file, so no
GFF-breakdown step is needed here.

```{r, load_files_real, include=FALSE}
rmout1 <- read.table(paste0(SIM1, 'processed_output.temp'), header = T, sep = '\t', comment.char = "") |>
  dplyr::mutate(div = as.numeric(1 - identity), identity_pct = as.numeric(identity) * 100)
rmout2 <- read.table(paste0(SIM2, 'processed_output.temp'), header = T, sep = '\t', comment.char = "") |>
  dplyr::mutate(div = as.numeric(1 - identity), identity_pct = as.numeric(identity) * 100)
rmout3 <- read.table(paste0(SIM3, 'processed_output.temp'), header = T, sep = '\t', comment.char = "") |>
  dplyr::mutate(div = as.numeric(1 - identity), identity_pct = as.numeric(identity) * 100)
rmout4 <- read.table(paste0(SIM4, 'processed_output.temp'), header = T, sep = '\t', comment.char = "") |>
  dplyr::mutate(div = as.numeric(1 - identity), identity_pct = as.numeric(identity) * 100)
rmout5 <- read.table(paste0(SIM5, 'processed_output.temp'), header = T, sep = '\t', comment.char = "") |>
  dplyr::mutate(div = as.numeric(1 - identity), identity_pct = as.numeric(identity) * 100)

genomes <- c("tair10", "rice", "maize", "dm6", "danio")
ori_list <- list(rmout1, rmout2, rmout3, rmout4, rmout5)
names(ori_list) <- genomes
```

## 2. Item 32: distribution fitting and goodness-of-fit

### 2.1 Family-level fitting (top `r TOP_N_FAMILY` families per superfamily)

Per-family fits cover the `r TOP_N_FAMILY` most abundant families (by copy number, N >=
`r MIN_FAMILY_N`) of each superfamily that holds >= `r MIN_SUPERFAMILY_PROP * 100`% of a
genome's loci. Class-only or unclassified labels ("DNA", "LTR", "Unknown", "*/unknown", "SINE?")
and non-TE repeats (satellites, simple repeats, rDNA, knobs, centromeric/subtelomeric repeats,
endogenous viruses) are left out of the per-family fits but stay in the genome-pooled fit
(section 2.2). Groups larger than `r format(MAX_FIT_N, big.mark = ",")` loci are fitted on a
random sample of that size (fixed seed); `n` is the full number of loci and `n_fit` the number
fitted.

Selecting the most abundant families favours families with many copies, which tend to have
smoother, more regular divergence distributions than rare families. The coverage table below
gives the share of each genome's loci that the selected families represent, so the scope of the
family-level results is explicit.

Reviewer 1 named maize Gypsy/Copia specifically - these are flagged separately in the summary
table (`superfamily` matches "Gypsy"/"Copia", case-insensitive) so they are easy to find without
scanning the full table.

```{r, gof_helpers, echo=FALSE}
# Fit on at most MAX_FIT_N loci; set.seed() per group, so the sample does not depend on
# which forked process or in which order the group is fitted
subsample_for_fit <- function(x){
  if (length(x) <= MAX_FIT_N) return(x)
  set.seed(FIT_SEED)
  sample(x, MAX_FIT_N)
}

# gof_table_for_group() reports n = length of the vector it fits; keep that as n_fit and
# report the full group size as n
gof_table_subsampled <- function(x, group, genome){
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  res <- gof_table_for_group(subsample_for_fit(x), group = group, genome = genome)
  if (is.null(res)) return(NULL)
  res |> dplyr::rename(n_fit = n) |> dplyr::mutate(n = length(x), .after = group)
}

excluded_superfamily <- function(sf){
  grepl(GENERIC_SF_REGEX, sf, ignore.case = TRUE) | grepl(NON_TE_SF_REGEX, sf, ignore.case = TRUE)
}

# One row per selected family: top TOP_N_FAMILY families (N >= MIN_FAMILY_N) of each
# retained superfamily
select_gof_families <- function(df){
  sf_counts <- df |> dplyr::count(superfamily, name = "sf_n") |> dplyr::mutate(sf_prop = sf_n / nrow(df))
  df |>
    dplyr::count(superfamily, family, name = "n") |>
    dplyr::left_join(sf_counts, by = "superfamily") |>
    dplyr::filter(!excluded_superfamily(superfamily), sf_prop >= MIN_SUPERFAMILY_PROP, n >= MIN_FAMILY_N) |>
    dplyr::group_by(superfamily) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(n, n = TOP_N_FAMILY, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

# mclapply returns try-error objects instead of stopping; surface them
check_mclapply <- function(res){
  failed <- vapply(res, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
  if (any(failed)) stop("parallel fit failed: ", paste(unlist(res[failed]), collapse = "\n"))
  res
}

gof_families <- lapply(ori_list, function(df){
  select_gof_families(df |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(div), !is.na(family), family != ""))
})
```

```{r, gof_family_coverage, echo=FALSE}
gof_coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genomes, function(g){
  df <- ori_list[[g]] |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(div))
  sel <- gof_families[[g]]
  retained_sf_loci <- sum(dplyr::distinct(sel, superfamily, sf_n)$sf_n)
  data.frame(genome = g,
             total_loci = nrow(df),
             n_superfamilies = dplyr::n_distinct(sel$superfamily),
             n_families = nrow(sel),
             loci_in_selected_families = sum(sel$n),
             pct_loci_covered = 100 * sum(sel$n) / nrow(df),
             loci_in_retained_superfamilies = retained_sf_loci,
             pct_of_retained_superfamilies = 100 * sum(sel$n) / retained_sf_loci)
}))
kable(gof_coverage, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
      caption = "Families selected for per-family fitting and the share of each genome's loci they cover.")
write.csv(gof_coverage, paste0(OUT, "gof_family_coverage.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Saved file name: gof_family_coverage.csv

```{r, gof_family_compute, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.extra = list(MIN_FAMILY_N, TOP_N_FAMILY, MIN_SUPERFAMILY_PROP, MAX_FIT_N, FIT_SEED, GENERIC_SF_REGEX, NON_TE_SF_REGEX)}
gof_family_results <- do.call(rbind, check_mclapply(parallel::mclapply(genomes, function(g){
  df <- ori_list[[g]] |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(div), !is.na(family), family != "")
  sel <- gof_families[[g]]

  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sel)), function(i){
    x <- df |> dplyr::filter(family == sel$family[i], superfamily == sel$superfamily[i]) |> dplyr::pull(div)
    res <- gof_table_subsampled(x, group = sel$family[i], genome = g)
    if (!is.null(res)) res$superfamily <- sel$superfamily[i]
    res
  }))
}, mc.cores = N_CORES)))

# Flag maize Gypsy/Copia rows for easy lookup
gof_family_results <- gof_family_results |>
  dplyr::mutate(flag_reviewer_named = genome == "maize" & grepl("Gypsy|Copia", superfamily, ignore.case = TRUE))

write.csv(gof_family_results, paste0(OUT, "gof_family_level.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, gof_family_table, echo=FALSE}
# used by the per-family plots (2.3) and the item 36 comparison (section 3)
maize_named_families <- gof_family_results |>
  dplyr::filter(flag_reviewer_named) |>
  dplyr::distinct(group) |>
  dplyr::pull(group)

# The full per-family table (3 rows per family) is too long to print; it is saved to
# gof_family_level.csv. Print a per-genome summary of the best-fitting distribution instead.
gof_family_best <- gof_family_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(genome, group, superfamily) |>
  dplyr::summarise(best = distribution[which.min(aic)],
                   delta_aic_norm = aic[distribution == "norm"][1] - min(aic),
                   ks_norm = ks_stat[distribution == "norm"][1],
                   ks_best = ks_stat[which.min(aic)], .groups = "drop")
gof_family_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(gof_family_best, gof_family_best |> dplyr::mutate(genome = "all")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(genome) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_families = dplyr::n(),
                   pct_best_norm = 100 * mean(best == "norm"),
                   pct_best_sn = 100 * mean(best == "sn"),
                   pct_best_gamma = 100 * mean(best == "gamma"),
                   pct_norm_delta_aic_gt10 = 100 * mean(delta_aic_norm > 10, na.rm = TRUE),
                   median_delta_aic_norm = median(delta_aic_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   median_ks_norm = median(ks_norm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   median_ks_best = median(ks_best, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(factor(genome, levels = c(genomes, "all")))
kable(gof_family_summary, digits = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 3),
      caption = paste0("Per-family goodness-of-fit summary (top ", TOP_N_FAMILY, " families per superfamily): ",
                        "share of families best fitted (lowest AIC) by each distribution, share where the ",
                        "Gaussian is > 10 AIC units worse than the best, and median KS statistics."))
write.csv(gof_family_summary, paste0(OUT, "gof_family_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Saved file names: gof_family_level.csv (full per-family table, not printed), gof_family_summary.csv

### 2.2 Genome-pooled fitting (all loci, including families not fitted individually)

```{r, gof_pooled_compute, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.extra = list(MIN_FAMILY_N, TOP_N_FAMILY, MIN_SUPERFAMILY_PROP, MAX_FIT_N, FIT_SEED, GENERIC_SF_REGEX, NON_TE_SF_REGEX)}
gof_pooled_results <- do.call(rbind, check_mclapply(parallel::mclapply(genomes, function(g){
  x <- ori_list[[g]] |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(div)) |> dplyr::pull(div)
  gof_table_subsampled(x, group = "(genome-pooled)", genome = g)
}, mc.cores = N_CORES)))

write.csv(gof_pooled_results, paste0(OUT, "gof_genome_pooled.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, gof_pooled_table, echo=FALSE}
kable(gof_pooled_results |> dplyr::arrange(genome, distribution), digits = 4,
      caption = "Goodness-of-fit (Gaussian vs. skew-normal vs. gamma) for whole-genome-pooled real divergence distributions.")
```

Saved file name: gof_genome_pooled.csv

### 2.3 Fit-overlay figures

One figure per genome-pooled distribution. Histograms show all loci; fitted curves come from
the same subsample used in section 2.2.

```{r, gof_plots_pooled, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.asp = .67, out.width="60%", results = "asis"}
for (g in genomes) {
  x <- ori_list[[g]] |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(div)) |> dplyr::pull(div)
  fits <- fit_divergence_distributions(subsample_for_fit(x))
  p <- plot_gof_overlay(x, fits, paste0("Genome: ", g, " (pooled, n=", length(x), ")"))

  png(filename = paste0(OUT, "gof_overlay_pooled_", g, ".png"), width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", res = 1200)
  print(p)
  while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()

  cat("\n\n#### ", g, " (pooled)\n\n")
  print(p)
  cat("\n\nSaved file name: gof_overlay_pooled_", g, ".png\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## 3. Item 36: former `identity_fix` adjustment, before/after comparison

`identity_fix` was applied by TEgenomeSimulator <= v1.0.0 and has since been removed (commit
`efa3369`): the current simulator mutates each copy with the raw Gaussian draw ("raw draw"
below), so "post-fix" is the former behaviour, kept here as the before/after evidence for
R2#3.

For each genome (pooled) and the maize Gypsy/Copia families named by Reviewer 1, draw simulated
identity values from `rnorm(mean_identity_pct, sd_identity_pct)` using that group's own real
mean/SD (the same statistic mode 2 would estimate), replicate `get_identity()`'s
resample-if-over-100 and truncate-to-integer behaviour (the current simulator also resamples
draws below 0, which never occur at these means/SDs), then apply the former `identity_fix`
transform and compare all three curves (real / raw draw / post-fix) on the percent-divergence
scale.

```{r, identity_fix_compute, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(20260917)  # reproducible draws; not a claim about the simulator's own RNG seeding

identity_fix_groups <- rbind(
  data.frame(genome = genomes, group = "(genome-pooled)", stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  data.frame(genome = "maize", group = maize_named_families, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
)

identity_fix_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(identity_fix_groups)), function(i){
  g <- identity_fix_groups$genome[i]
  grp <- identity_fix_groups$group[i]

  df <- ori_list[[g]]
  real_pct <- if (grp == "(genome-pooled)") {
    df |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(identity_pct)) |> dplyr::pull(identity_pct)
  } else {
    df |> dplyr::filter(family == grp, is.finite(identity_pct)) |> dplyr::pull(identity_pct)
  }

  n_sim <- min(length(real_pct), 5000)  # cap for speed on the largest genomes (e.g. danio)
  sim_draws <- simulate_identity_draws(n_sim, mean(real_pct), stats::sd(real_pct))

  p <- plot_identity_fix_comparison(real_pct, sim_draws,
                                     paste0(g, ": ", grp, " (n_real=", length(real_pct), ", n_sim=", n_sim, ")"))
  # legend: "raw draw" is the current simulator, "post identity_fix" the former (<= v1.0.0) adjustment
  p <- suppressMessages(p + scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Real (empirical)" = "grey40",
               "Simulated (raw Gaussian draw)" = "#336699",
               "Simulated (post identity_fix)" = "#CC3333"),
    labels = c("Real (empirical)" = "Real (RepeatMasker)",
               "Simulated (raw Gaussian draw)" = "Gaussian draw (TEGS)",
               "Simulated (post identity_fix)" = "Identity_fix (dnvTEe)")))
  safe_grp <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", grp)
  png(filename = paste0(OUT, "identity_fix_comparison_", g, "_", safe_grp, ".png"), width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", res = 1200)
  print(p)
  while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()

  data.frame(
    genome = g,
    group = grp,
    n_real = length(real_pct),
    mean_identity_real = mean(real_pct),
    sd_identity_real = stats::sd(real_pct),
    mean_identity_raw_draw = mean(sim_draws$raw),
    sd_identity_raw_draw = stats::sd(sim_draws$raw),
    mean_identity_post_fix = mean(sim_draws$post_fix),
    sd_identity_post_fix = stats::sd(sim_draws$post_fix),
    ks_real_vs_raw = unname(suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(real_pct, sim_draws$raw)$statistic)),
    ks_real_vs_post_fix = unname(suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(real_pct, sim_draws$post_fix)$statistic))
  )
}))
rownames(identity_fix_summary) <- NULL

write.csv(identity_fix_summary, paste0(OUT, "identity_fix_comparison_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, identity_fix_table, echo=FALSE}
kable(identity_fix_summary, digits = 3,
      caption = paste0("Mean/SD of real identity vs. simulated raw Gaussian draw (current simulator) vs. ",
                        "post-identity_fix draw (former adjustment, <= v1.0.0), and KS statistic of each ",
                        "simulated distribution against the real one. identity_fix is a fixed affine transform ",
                        "(y = 0.5x + 50), so it halves the SD and shifts the mean toward 100 without changing ",
                        "distribution shape - it does not address any tail-heaviness/skewness gap, it only ",
                        "narrows and relocates the (still-Gaussian) draw."))
```

Saved file name: identity_fix_comparison_summary.csv

## 4. Notes / caveats for the manuscript response

- The empirical divergence data used for both the GOF fitting (section 2) and the
  `identity_fix` comparison (section 3) is itself measured by RepeatMasker on the real genomes.
  RepeatMasker's detection sensitivity is known to decline at high divergence, so this empirical
  distribution is likely right-censored - it probably under-represents the most divergent,
  hardest-to-detect relics. Any deviation from Gaussian reported here should therefore be read
  as a conservative (lower-bound) estimate of the true mismatch between the Gaussian assumption
  and real biology.
- KS statistics in section 2 are reported without p-values, since `gofstat()`'s asymptotic KS
  null distribution assumes known (not MLE-fitted) parameters. AIC/BIC (which do not have this
  issue) are the primary basis for ranking the three candidate distributions; the KS statistic
  is reported as a descriptive effect-size alongside them.
- `identity_fix` (item 36) was a deterministic affine transform of the raw Gaussian draw
  (`y = 0.5x + 50`), so it was analytically still Gaussian - it could not fix a shape mismatch
  (skewness/heavy tail) reported in section 2; it only shifted and narrowed the draw. Section 3's
  summary table confirms this empirically (post-fix SD ~= 0.5 x raw-draw SD), and shows the
  post-fix draw sits much further from the real distribution than the raw draw. The adjustment
  was therefore removed from the simulator (commit `efa3369`, after v1.0.0); all revised
  simulations use the raw draw, and the identity in the output GFF is the identity used to
  mutate the copy.
- Per-family fits cover only the `r TOP_N_FAMILY` most abundant families of each retained
  superfamily (`r round(min(gof_coverage$pct_loci_covered))`-`r round(max(gof_coverage$pct_loci_covered))`%
  of each genome's loci; see the coverage table in section 2.1). Abundant families tend to have
  smoother, more regular divergence distributions than rare ones, so the family-level results
  describe the families that dominate each genome rather than every family. The genome-pooled
  fits (section 2.2) use all loci.
- Groups with more than `r format(MAX_FIT_N, big.mark = ",")` loci are fitted on a random
  sample of that size (fixed seed); at that sample size the AIC/BIC ranking and the KS
  statistic are stable, and the full n is reported alongside n_fit.
